nodes.description: Prolonged chloramphenicol exposure produces a neurotoxicity - optic neuritis, often with peripheral neuropathy - separate from the acute neonatal syndrome. Across the reported cases it follows prolonged, high-cumulative-dose therapy (mean ~229 days and ~255 g at the time of neurologic findings), which is the discriminator that sets this chronic arm apart from the acute toxidrome. Its mechanism is not established; direct neurotoxicity, hypersensitivity and vitamin B deficiency have all been proposed, and the vitamin-deficiency hypothesis underlies the B12/B6 treatment sometimes used. It is therefore placed off the exposure node rather than the mitochondrial chain.
